concepts.def: Heinrich Schenker's Der freie Satz 1935; reductive analysis revealing Ursatz background, middleground and foreground.
Allen Forte's Structure of Atonal Music 1973 catalogued unordered pitch-class sets in atonal works; prime forms and interval vectors.
William Caplin's Classical Form 1998 categorises beginning-middle-end thematic functions in sonata-form themes.
David Lewin's Generalized Musical Intervals 1987 and Richard Cohn 1996; PLR transformations track chromatic chord relations.
Leonard Ratner's Classic Music 1980 catalogued late-18th-century topoi (military, pastoral, sturm und drang) as semantic markers.
Eric Clarke's Ways of Listening 2005 and CHARM project Mazurka analyses since 2004; empirical study of recorded performances.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1973 Structure of Atonal Music codified set classes?
options: Forte
Lewin
Babbitt
Rahn

mcqs.q: Whose 1998 Classical Form defines thematic functions?
options: Caplin
Hepokoski
Webster
Rosen

mcqs.q: What is a balanced antecedent-consequent phrase?
options: Two phrases of equal length where the first sounds open (question) and the second resolves (answer).
Any two phrases of similar style.
A long melody with no breaks.
Adjusting volume electronically.

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
They are the same scale.
A long melody with no breaks.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.

mcqs.q: What does modulation mean in music?
options: Changing from one key to another within a piece.
A long melody with no breaks.
Changing tempo or dynamics.
Adjusting volume electronically.

sequence.def: Begins c.500: monks sing unaccompanied plainchant
c.1600-1750: harpsichord continuo and terraced dynamics
c.1750-1820: elegant balance; the piano replaces the harpsichord
c.1820-1900: rubato, chromatic harmony, huge orchestras
After 1900: serialism, minimalism and electronics arrive
